items.notes: Terms as described by the host government; cross-check ZDF (Dominik Rzepka). Closes watch W-261115-03.
items.text: [[p:Friedrich Merz]] hosted the [[p:Coalition of the willing (Russo-Ukrainian war)|coalition of the willing]] in Berlin with leaders from about 37 countries, [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and US envoys [[p:Jared Kushner]] and [[p:Steve Witkoff]]. The German government says members agreed to back Ukraine into 2027 and want four-way talks (Ukraine, Russia, the US and a European team of the EU institutions plus France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK), with territorial talks starting from the line of contact and sanctions eased only step by step. Merz cited broad support for a proposed extra €45bn in aid for 2027, not yet approved.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: ISW adds that Putin rejected European security guarantees and foreign troops, and that Ukraine hit an oil pumping station at Almetyevsk.
items.text: Ukraine struck the [[p:Crimean Bridge]] for the third time in four days, halting rail traffic for several hours. [[p:Vladimir Putin]] said the road section was seriously damaged, called the bridge civilian infrastructure and vowed a response; Ukraine's Defence Ministry said Russia would now have to supply its forces overland.

items.notes: Houthi claim of targets is theirs; tower damage reported by Gulf News; Sanaa strikes per Times of Israel liveblog.
items.text: The [[p:Houthis]] said they fired cruise missiles at Riyadh's airport and financial district; early on 19 Nov the [[p:Public Investment Fund]] tower in Riyadh was damaged, and the Saudi-led coalition said it had dealt with a missile threat. Saudi-led forces then reportedly struck Sanaa. Separately, a tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile north of Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz on 18 Nov; its crew is safe.

items.notes: The PMF brigades reportedly include some Kata'ib Hezbollah fighters. Closes watch W-261117-01.
items.text: Baghdad and [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]] averted a showdown over Jurf al-Sakhar: from 20 Nov a joint operations centre and a combined force of army, federal police, Energy Police and [[p:Popular Mobilization Forces]] brigades take over the stronghold. An Iraqi official says Quds Force commander [[p:Esmail Qaani]] came to Iraq to push for the deal.

items.notes: Chemical-weapons claim is Israel's; disputed by Iran. The USS George Washington has reportedly left the region, leaving two US carriers.
items.text: Israel sent its Mossad chief to Washington with intelligence it says shows Iran advancing a chemical weapons programme. [[p:Donald Trump]] told Fox News there was an indication of this and threatened a harsh response, hinting action might not come before 1 January; Iran's Foreign Ministry called the claims fabricated, and some US officials reportedly doubt the intelligence.

items.notes: Claim rests on Chinese state media; no independent confirmation of the wording.
items.text: [[p:Xinhua News Agency|Xinhua]] reported that Trump told [[p:Xi Jinping]] in Shenzhen that the US does not support Taiwan independence. Taiwan's [[p:Mainland Affairs Council]] called the report untrue and asked Washington to clarify; no US statement had followed.

items.notes: Outcome pending at time of logging; watch W-261108-01.
items.text: On the eve of the scheduled close of [[e:COP31|2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] in Antalya, the presidency's revised draft dropped all explicit language on moving away from fossil fuels and a proposed $120bn yearly adaptation-finance target. Campaigners called it a step back; EU ministers had not taken a position, and overtime was possible.

items.notes: Al-Khuwai (13 Nov) and the Abu Zabad airstrike were logged in E-261117-06. Army territorial claims not independently verified.
items.text: The army said it took Al-Saatat, northeast of Abu Zabad, putting troops about 60 km from RSF-held En Nahud. [[p:Armed Conflict Location and Event Data|ACLED]] counts more than 30 villages and towns in North and West Kordofan retaken by the army and allies, helped by defections of [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] commanders.

A UN Human Rights Office report found drones caused over 1,630 of the 2,230 civilian deaths it verified from January to October, and Kordofan accounted for over two-thirds of documented casualties. It logged 29 RSF drone strikes on power and fuel sites in 11 states between 20 Oct and 4 Nov; [[p:Volker Türk]] condemned both parties' disregard for the laws of war.

items.notes: Article page could not be opened directly; details via a summary of it. RSF claim; Nyala strike single-source (https://sudantribune.com/article/321451).
items.text: The RSF says it seized Bau locality in Blue Nile after an army force withdrew towards Ed Damazin; activists say fighting displaced 1,409 families from Wad al-Mahi, Bau and Geissan. Sudan Tribune also reports army strikes on an RSF headquarters in Nyala.

items.notes: Cross-check headline only. Emergency Lawyers urged handover of Haroun and Omar al-Bashir to the ICC.
items.text: The military detained [[p:Ahmed Haroun]], head of the former ruling [[p:National Congress Party (Sudan)|National Congress Party]] and wanted by the [[p:International Criminal Court]], in Omdurman, his lawyers said. No reason was given; they linked it to a podcast in which he said his party and the army were united against the RSF.
Sudan lifted its 20-month ban on Kenyan tea, imposed over Nairobi's hosting of RSF figures; [[p:William Ruto]] credited talks with Prime Minister [[p:Kamil Idris]].

items.notes: Clashes unconfirmed by Reuters; ACLED said Eritrea regained Badme on 15 Nov. Addis Standard piece on Badme clashes could not be opened.
items.text: ACLED and the [[p:International Crisis Group]] say Ethiopian and Eritrean forces are massed within striking distance along the border. Ethiopian drones reportedly hit Eritrean positions near Badme on 12 Nov, Eritrean artillery replied, and the armies reportedly clashed on 13 Nov; Reuters could not confirm the clashes. Eritrea's information minister [[p:Yemane Gebremeskel]] dismissed Ethiopian claims as propaganda, and G7 foreign ministers urged restraint.

items.notes: Accusations are the Ethiopian government's. Anadolu link not read.
items.text: Army chief Field Marshal Birhanu Jula visited Mekelle for the first time since the war resumed, accused the [[p:Tigray People's Liberation Front]] of seeking secession with Eritrea's help, and on 14 Nov accused Eritrea of leading the rebel offensive and Egypt of arming it. Eritrea denies sending forces. A UN and ambassadors' delegation, including the US ambassador, visited Mekelle on 17–18 Nov.

[[p:Fano (militia)|Fano]] forces say they seized Debre Werq southeast of Bahir Dar, after federal forces reportedly retook towns on the A2 highway earlier in November; suspected OLA fighters killed a ruling-party official in North Shewa on 9 Nov.

Federal forces took over the Supreme Court building and a new chief justice, Ibrahim Idle Suleiman, was installed; the opposition Somali Future Council called it a coup against the court. On 9 Nov the attorney general said the government rejects the 5 Nov ruling against President [[p:Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]'s term extension as legally void, arguing institutions stay in office until May 2027.

The Somali Future Council boycotted the president's 14–18 Nov election talks, saying it no longer recognises him and wants the US, UK, EU and Türkiye to mediate. Blocs of former president Farmaajo and former PM Sharmarke accepted in principle; no report showed the talks convening.

In a televised address, Hassan Sheikh accused the UAE of interference, building parallel armed forces and signing port deals without federal approval, and linked it to Israel's recognition of Somaliland. UAE adviser [[p:Anwar Gargash]] called him the outgoing president; Somalia's defence minister urged prosecuting alleged UAE collaborators.

In Hiiraan, Hawadle clan leaders called for mobilisation and more federal troops reportedly defected to Beledweyne; the president offered on 8 Nov to move Hirshabelle's capital to Hiiraan, which ex-intelligence chief Sanbaloolshe rejected.

The election commission told AFP the first post-independence elections move from 22 Dec 2026 to 11 Feb 2027, as voter registration was due to start; President [[p:Salva Kiir Mayardit|Salva Kiir]] confirmed he will run for the [[p:Sudan People's Liberation Movement|SPLM]].

The High Court acquitted opposition leader [[p:Tundu Lissu]] of treason but convicted him of incitement and jailed him for four years, after 19 months in detention; he can appeal. The EU and US raised concerns.

Army chief [[p:Muhoozi Kainerugaba]] said on 6 Nov he would hand over as defence chief within months, deactivated his X account on 10 Nov after posts threatening Vice-President [[p:Jessica Alupo]], and on 17 Nov declared he will seek the presidency after his father.
In his last State of the Nation address of his first term, Ruto proposed exempting low earners from income tax, scrapping stamp duty on small land deals and removing import duty on phones.
President [[p:Ismaïl Omar Guelleh]] named Aden Ali Mahamade defence minister, filling a post vacant since July.

items.notes: Some outlets call the movement "Force de résistance nationale"; majority local usage is FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation). Uvira–Fizi fighting per L'Interview.cd.
items.text: Fighters of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation led by [[p:Joseph Kabila]] pushed through Kahuzi-Biega park, taking Kalonge and Bitale on 7 Nov and Bulambika on 8 Nov, raising fears of an advance on the Walikale axis; the army says it retook Katasomwa. OCHA counted over 323,000 people displaced in Kalehe and Kabare between 6 and 9 Nov, and fighting spread to the Uvira–Fizi highlands from 10 Nov.

The [[p:Organisation internationale de la Francophonie]] summit in Phnom Penh postponed electing a secretary-general to late 2027 after Kinshasa threatened to quit if Rwanda's [[p:Louise Mushikiwabo]] won a third term; she stays on meanwhile.
Eleven opposition parties said they will back President [[p:Évariste Ndayishimiye]] and the ruling [[p:CNDD–FDD]] in the May 2027 presidential vote; nominations close on 22 Nov.
